links.outcome: Effect of reweighting and equalized-odds mitigation on fairness metrics and prediction performance by race
links.effect: For race, reweighting worsened outcomes for the under-represented group and increased unfairness; equalized-odds post-processing improved results for the under-represented group with significant fairness gains.
links.quote: In the case of the most severe bias (race), the pre-trained logistic regression model using the reweighting algorithm shows some deterioration in prediction outcomes for the under-represented group and even an increase in unfairness, while the post-processing approach improves results for the under-represented group and provides significant fairness gains.

links.outcome: Subgroup performance and fairness gaps by race and gender in glioma grading models
links.effect: Demographic bias was found in glioma grading classifiers, with race showing the most severe bias.
links.quote: In the case of the most severe bias (race), the pre-trained logistic regression model using the reweighting algorithm shows some deterioration in prediction outcomes for the under-represented group and even an increase in unfairness, while the post-processing approach improves results for the under-represented group and provides significant fairness gains.

screen.practice: bias mitigation (reweighting and equalized odds post-processing)
screen.reason: Evaluates the impact and trade-offs of specific bias mitigation practices (pre-processing reweighting vs post-processing equalized odds) on model fairness and performance using clinical dataset benchmarks.
